title: What is known about 1RB1RA_0LC0RA_1RC1LD_0LB1LE_1LF0RC_---0LD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RA_0LC0RA_1RC1LD_0LB1LE_1LF0RC_---0LD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The run is a sequence of rounds, each starting from W (100)k 10 (110)N 111 B> with a short word W. Lean proves the sweep rules the rounds are built from; a symbolic run in Python checks the inner period of a round for all sizes. The round map itself is found by simulation only, and no rule that decides it is known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 33,249 cells have been visited and 21,631 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.488). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.052).

claims.title: Twelve sweep rules, for all n
claims.text: The head crosses a run of n copies of a word (110, 100, 010, 011, 10, 01 or 1) in one go, for all n and any tape around it; for example L B> (110)n R becomes L (011)n B> R in 3n steps. These are the building blocks of every round.

claims.title: The marker period, for all sizes
claims.text: A symbolic run (for all k, x, y at once) from D> 0 b 1 0 1 a bk 1 0 ax+27 1 a 0 ay (a = 110, b = 100) reaches the same shape with k + 3, x and y + 27 in exactly 324k + 162x + 3629 steps. The Lean theorem the same run produces is too large for the kernel so far, so this rests on the Python tool.

claims.title: The run is made of rounds
claims.text: A C run from blank tape to 1.6 × 1010 steps passes 54 round starts 0∞ W (100)k 10 (110)N 111 B> 0∞; the last ones have N = 26,972, 43,155 and 69,047.

claims.title: No synthetic round halts
claims.text: About 20,000 rounds started from the words W seen in the run and arbitrary k ≤ 80, N ≤ 600 all reach a next round start; none halts. The set of words W reachable this way is not closed (thousands of new ones appear), so this is not a closed-set argument.

claims.title: The marker period, for all sizes
claims.text: A symbolic run (for all k, x, y at once) from D> 0 b 1 0 1 a bk 1 0 ax+27 1 a 0 ay (a = 110, b = 100) reaches the same shape with k + 3, x and y + 27 in exactly 324k + 162x + 3629 steps. The Lean theorem the same run produces is too large for the kernel so far, so this rests on the Python tool.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A proof would need the round map on (W, k, N) in closed form and then an argument about its orbit; neither is done.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine works in rounds: it keeps two runs of three-cell words, 100s on the left and 110s on the right, and in each round a small marker sweeps through the 110s, converting them in batches of 27. Round after round the numbers grow, and sometimes the 100s are all used up and the count restarts. This page runs the real machine, shows a round, and lists what is known.

facts.text: The marker passes 27 words 110 and adds three words 100 on each period.
Round starts seen in 1.6 × 10<sup>10</sup> steps from blank tape.
No halt in the C simulator.

sections.heading: Two runs of three-cell words
html:
Write a = 110 and b = 100. Each round starts when the head, in state B, extends the tape to the right of

0∞ W bk 1 0 aN 1 1 1 B> 0∞
where W is a short word that starts with 1 (10, 10101110, 101001011010, …). The left part W bk works like one counter, roughly 9k plus a value read from W, and N is a second counter.

sections.heading: A marker sweeping the 110s
html:
During a round a marker 1 a 0 = 11100 sits inside the run of a's. The head shuttles between the left end and the marker; in the main phase of the round, each period carries 27 a's from the left of the marker to its right and writes three new b's at the left end of the tape. A symbolic run checks this period for all sizes at once (py/gen_period.py, 324k + 162x + 3629 steps); the sweeps it is made of are proved in Lean (lean/Rules.lean):

D> 0 b 1 0 1 a bk 1 0 ax+27 1 a 0 ay
  →  D> 0 b 1 0 1 a bk+3 1 0 ax 1 a 0 ay+27

Before the main phase the old b's are converted, and when fewer than 27 a's are left the remainder, together with the old W, decides the next W, k and N. Usually k and N grow by about 10% a round; in a reset round the b's are used up, k drops to 0, the word becomes 10101110 (or a short relative) and N grows by a factor of about 1.65.

sections.heading: Round starts from blank tape
html: Resets (k = 0) happen for example at N = 27, 60, 1016, 6001, 9905 and 16345. A round with N words costs on the order of N2 steps, so the tape grows like the square root of the step count on the left, as the first look found.

sections.heading: How it would halt
html: The only halting transition is F0: the head, in state F, reads a 0. This happens only when the head in state D comes onto a 1 that has 00 to its left, for example the leftmost 1 of the tape; inside a well-formed round this never happens. A halt would need a round whose left word W, together with the remainder of the a's, produces such a pattern.

No round seen in the run, and none of about 20,000 synthetic rounds, halts. What is missing is the round map in closed form: the effect of the 27-period remainder on W and on the next counters, and then an argument (or a Collatz-type heuristic) about the orbit of that map.

summary: Rounds of the form W (100)^k 10 (110)^N 111 B>, a marker 11100 sweeping the 110-run 27 words at a time; the round map on (W, k, N) is mapped out but not solved. Open.
